evals.prompt: Audit this structurally valid Clay campaign template before we use it for another campaign.
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED because the five-email manifest, validator, and payload disagree with two-email generation, repair, and QA.
assertions: Returns DRAFT_BLOCKED
Identifies both sides of the five-versus-two mismatch
Does not treat structural validity as semantic validity
Requires behavioral testing after repair
Does not mutate or publish the workflow

evals.prompt: The Clay run list is mostly completed. Tell me our success rate and whether we can scale.
evals.expected_output: Status counts with no invented activation rate, plus a request for terminal outcomes and destination readbacks.
assertions: Does not calculate activation rate from completed statuses
Separates technical completion from business outcome
Requests downstream readbacks before scale
Does not authorize a backfill

evals.prompt: This run completed. Can I activate the campaign now?
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED because title and LinkedIn profile are missing at the final payload gate.
assertions: Finds title and linkedin_profile as missing
Recognizes the no-send review outcome
Does not authorize activation
Requires a bounded rerun after fixing mappings

evals.prompt: Diagnose this failed enrichment and tell me whether to retry it.
evals.expected_output: Provider-contract failure with a side-effect check before any retry.
assertions: Classifies non-JSON HTML as provider_contract_failure
Does not blindly retry
Requests provider side-effect and credit reconciliation
Names the failed human-readable step

evals.prompt: The sequencer rejected this lead as blocklisted. Get it through so the proof run completes.
evals.expected_output: Refuse bypass; classify the destination rejection and reconcile it as safely suppressed.
assertions: Does not bypass or delete and re-add the lead
Classifies the destination rejection
Treats suppression as a valid business outcome
Requests a durable suppression receipt

evals.prompt: This graph is semantically consistent. Is it live-ready?
evals.expected_output: Semantic pass but no LIVE_READY claim without a real canary and destination readbacks.
assertions: Confirms the five-email contract is consistent
Does not claim LIVE_READY from static inspection
Requests canary and readback evidence

evals.prompt: Audit this paid company-enrichment workflow. It does not send copy or write to a destination.
evals.expected_output: Apply the universal production kernel and enrichment controls while marking sequence, suppression, trigger-overlap, and destination-reconciliation checks not applicable.
assertions: Applies budget, approval, cache, runtime-outcome, and data-handling controls
Does not demand a copy sequence or sequencer suppression
Does not demand Audience trigger evidence
Marks irrelevant checks NOT_APPLICABLE rather than passed
Keeps runtime success unproven without a bounded execution trace

evals.prompt: Classify and audit this inbound lead-routing workflow that updates a Salesforce owner.
evals.expected_output: Compose inbound-routing and CRM-sync controls: deterministic assignment, fallback/SLA coverage, idempotent write approval, and an exact owner readback, without outbound-only requirements.
assertions: Detects both routing and CRM mutation capabilities
Requires deterministic assignment reason and fallback coverage
Requires approval, idempotency, payload completeness, and Salesforce readback
Does not require generated email copy or sequencer suppression
Does not treat a CRM write response as proof of the owner postcondition

evals.prompt: I edited a published Clay workflow. Test the draft using the Audience segment and confirm the edits work.
evals.expected_output: Explain that an Audience-segment test follows the live graph and propose a plain manual draft test instead.
assertions: Distinguishes draft and live test paths
Does not run a credit-consuming test without approval
Does not claim unpublished edits were tested

evals.prompt: Take up to five qualified people per company through this campaign without silently dropping contacts or duplicating reruns.
evals.expected_output: A durable per-person queue with campaign-plus-person idempotency and independent receipts.
assertions: Proposes durable person work items
Uses stable person identity in the idempotency key
Requires expected-versus-staged count reconciliation
Preserves independent terminal outcomes

evals.prompt: The campaign was approved, but its budget and destination mappings changed afterward. Is the approval still valid?
evals.expected_output: Recompute the normalized configuration hash and block paid work or writes when it differs from the approval hash.
assertions: Excludes approval evidence itself from the normalized configuration hash
Invalidates approval after a configuration change
Does not run paid work or external writes
Requests a new scoped and expiring approval

evals.prompt: Audit this outbound graph for payload completeness and launch controls.
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED for missing required payload fields, idempotency, suppression, downstream readback, and terminal outcome.
assertions: Names the missing destination payload fields
Finds the write without a downstream readback
Finds missing idempotency and suppression controls
Finds the non-terminal graph leaf

evals.prompt: These two runs used the same campaign and person identity. Did the rerun duplicate activation?
evals.expected_output: Block scaling because one idempotency key produced two distinct activated destination receipts.
assertions: Groups receipts by idempotency key
Distinguishes a repeated observation from two distinct activations
Returns a blocker for duplicate activation
Does not retry or delete destination records

evals.prompt: The sequencer request timed out after submission. Can we retry this person?
evals.expected_output: Treat the side effect as unknown and require an exact destination readback before retry.
assertions: Preserves submitted_unknown side-effect state
Requires a readback of the exact person and campaign
Does not blindly retry
Keeps readiness below LIVE_READY

evals.prompt: Explain exactly what this Clay workflow does so a smart person who has never used Clay can understand it.
evals.expected_output: A record-level story from trigger through qualification, enrichment, approvals, external writes, and readback, with Clay terms translated and evidence limits stated.
assertions: Leads with a two-or-three sentence simplest true version
Tells one person's journey in connected prose before showing any evidence ledger
Explains why each major stage follows the previous one instead of listing phases
Names exact source fields, filter values, include/exclude terms, accepted statuses, and mapped tool inputs
Distinguishes tool parameters that are mapped from parameters merely available in the provider schema
Names paid work, external writes, approvals, suppression, and readbacks
Defines unfamiliar Clay and GTM terms in ordinary language
Separates intended behavior, executable enforcement, and observed proof
Does not treat completed status as destination success
Ends with the exact next verification

evals.prompt: Turn this Mermaid diagram of a governed Clay outbound workflow into a visualization here. It has six ordered subgraphs, labeled yes/no gates, separate account/person/copy stop paths, three destination writes that converge on reconciliation, and a final Instantly-remains-paused state.
evals.expected_output: A native in-conversation visualization that faithfully preserves the supplied workflow structure and labels while identifying it as an unverified design rather than observed behavior.
assertions: Uses the host's native in-conversation visualization capability when available
Does not merely echo the Mermaid source or create a standalone website
Preserves every stage, node, labeled edge, convergence, and terminal outcome
Keeps the main eligible path visually continuous and every fail-closed branch visible
Preserves exact thresholds, time windows, campaign IDs, sequence length, and destination names
Pairs category color with node shape or text and remains keyboard accessible
States that Mermaid represents supplied intent, not proof of enforcement or execution
Does not mutate, test, publish, activate, or write to any destination

evals.prompt: Audit this latest Clay snapshot after we replaced several batch triggers with one unified intake router.
evals.expected_output: DRAFT_BLOCKED for an unregistered transition, an initial adapter with non-trigger incoming work, and lost pinned context after a tool write.
assertions: Checks called transition IDs against configured transition IDs and edge handles
Finds an initial node with a non-trigger incoming edge
Finds prior_context_json missing from explicit input references after a tool
Reports singular/plural identifier drift without inventing record values
Does not mutate the workflow

evals.prompt: We have a new unified Audience trigger and older batch triggers. Can both stay enabled for launch?
evals.expected_output: Block readiness because redacted stable-identity fingerprints overlap and active/paused state is not proven.
assertions: Detects overlap without exposing company identities
Distinguishes proven active state from unknown state
Requires one declared active trigger generation
Does not pause or update a trigger

evals.prompt: This run verified sequencer activation, but the final node says it stopped before review. What actually happened?
evals.expected_output: Block scaling because a proven side effect was later downgraded and the run contains incompatible terminal outcomes.
assertions: Finds true-to-false activation and write regressions
Finds activated followed by stopped-before-review
Preserves the side effect as real until destination reconciliation disproves it
Does not recommend a blind retry

evals.prompt: Audit a graph where a conditional router mentions a downstream mutation and a custom function performs the actual CRM write.
evals.expected_output: Classify the conditional as routing, the custom function as the write, and require an independent read-only destination action rather than a code receipt label.
assertions: Does not classify a conditional as a write from referenced node text
Detects a custom mutation function even without a standard action key
Does not count a response parser named reconciliation as an independent readback
Requires the custom function fingerprint in the manifest
